domain: Theological Ethics / Technology Governance / Political Theology
topic_summary: Papal encyclical Magnifica Humanitas addresses safeguarding human dignity in the AI era through Catholic Social Doctrine. The document frames technological transformation as a choice between two biblical paradigms: the Tower of Babel (technocratic dominance, uniformity, self-sufficiency) versus the rebuilding of Jerusalem (shared responsibility, subsidiarity, communion). It applies principles of common good, universal destination of goods, subsidiarity, solidarity, and social justice to AI governance, work transformation, communication ecology, and peace-building.

key_entities: Catholic Church / Magisterium (authoritative interpreter of Gospel implications for social order)
AI systems / digital platforms (technological infrastructure reshaping communication, work, power)
Technocratic paradigm (efficiency-first logic detached from human dignity)
Transhumanism / posthumanism (ideological currents seeking human enhancement or transcendence)
Nation-states (traditional governance actors with eroding capacity vs. digital power)
Private technological actors (corporations controlling data, algorithms, platforms)
Workers / vulnerable populations (those bearing costs of automation, surveillance, exclusion)
Multilateral institutions (UN, international law frameworks under strain)
Tower of Babel archetype (self-sufficient power, uniformity, dehumanization)
Jerusalem rebuilding archetype (shared responsibility, subsidiarity, communion)
Grace / Christian humanism (theological alternative to technological transcendence)
Civilization of love (Paul VI's framework for social order grounded in charity and justice)
key_tensions: Technological power concentration (private actors) vs. democratic accountability and common good governance
Efficiency-driven automation vs. dignity of work and human agency
AI as neutral tool vs. AI as embodiment of designers' values and power structures
Transhumanist enhancement narrative vs. Christian acceptance of human limits as site of grace

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The authority of Catholic Social Doctrine to adjudicate legitimate social and technological order rests on fidelity to the Gospel and Tradition as interpreted by the Magisterium, particularly the principle that human dignity is inalienable, ontological, and grounded in being created in the image of the Triune God.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: The Magisterium (papal teaching, conciliar documents, theological tradition) interprets the Gospel's implications for social life. Legitimacy derives from apostolic succession and claimed continuity with revealed truth, not from democratic mandate or technocratic expertise.

readings.commitment: AI governance legitimacy derives from conformity to Catholic Social Doctrine principles (common good, subsidiarity, solidarity, universal destination of goods) as authoritatively interpreted by the Magisterium. Technology must be subordinated to these principles through transparent accountability, participatory governance, and protection of the vulnerable.
readings.authority_grounding: Magisterial tradition from Leo XIII through Francis; Gospel anthropology; natural law accessible to reason but illuminated by faith
readings.expected_structural_delta: High ε (0.45–0.55). Beneficiaries: workers, Global South, families, marginalized populations. Victims of non-compliance: private tech monopolies, military-industrial complex, extractive finance. Constraint type: tangled_rope (entangles efficiency with dignity; subsidiarity with solidarity). Enforcement: moral suasion, civil society pressure, international law advocacy, ecclesial witness. The encyclical explicitly rejects pure technocratic or market logics and demands political oversight grounded in human dignity.

readings.commitment: AI governance legitimacy derives from maximizing aggregate welfare, efficiency, and innovation. Ethical constraints are secondary optimization parameters. Authority rests with technical expertise and demonstrated performance. The encyclical's principles are aspirational values to be balanced against feasibility and growth imperatives.
readings.authority_grounding: Utilitarian ethics; economic growth models; Silicon Valley innovation culture; technocratic governance traditions
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate ε (0.30–0.40). Beneficiaries: tech firms, investors, high-skill workers, early adopters. Victims: displaced workers, communities lacking digital infrastructure, those profiled by opaque algorithms. Constraint type: rope (coordination around efficiency metrics). Enforcement: market competition, regulatory capture, expert consensus. This reading treats dignity as a constraint on optimization rather than the optimization target itself.

readings.commitment: AI governance legitimacy derives from democratic deliberation and consent of the governed. No single tradition (religious or technocratic) holds interpretive monopoly. Principles emerge from inclusive public reason, balancing diverse values through transparent political processes. The encyclical contributes one voice among many.
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal democratic theory; Rawlsian public reason; human rights frameworks; constitutional pluralism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate ε (0.35–0.45). Beneficiaries: civil society organizations, democratic institutions, minority rights holders. Victims: those excluded from deliberative processes, populations under authoritarian regimes. Constraint type: scaffold (builds participatory infrastructure). Enforcement: electoral accountability, judicial review, civil liberties protections. This reading accepts the encyclical's dignity claims but denies the Magisterium's unique authority to interpret them.

readings.commitment: AI governance legitimacy derives from voluntary exchange and property rights. Innovation flourishes when unencumbered by collective mandates. Dignity is protected through exit options and competitive markets, not centralized oversight. The encyclical's subsidiarity principle supports decentralization but its solidarity demands constitute illegitimate coercion.
readings.authority_grounding: Lockean property rights; Austrian economics; libertarian political philosophy; spontaneous order theory
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low ε (0.20–0.30). Beneficiaries: entrepreneurs, investors, high-autonomy individuals. Victims: those lacking market power, communities facing coordination failures, workers in monopsony labor markets. Constraint type: mountain (claims property rights as pre-political). Enforcement: contract law, private arbitration, reputational mechanisms. This reading rejects the encyclical's claim that economic freedom must be subordinated to common good as defined by political authority.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Magisterial reading holds human dignity as the non-negotiable optimization target (persons are ends, never means); technocratic reading treats dignity as one constraint among others in a welfare maximization function. No single framework can hold both 'dignity is the measure of all else' and 'dignity is measured against efficiency gains' as simultaneously true.

Magisterial reading asserts economic freedom is subordinate to common good as defined by solidarity and universal destination of goods (property has intrinsic social function); libertarian reading asserts property rights are pre-political and immune to collective redefinition. No coherent framework can hold both 'all property serves the common good by nature' and 'property rights precede and constrain common good claims.'

Democratic reading denies any tradition's monopoly on interpreting dignity (legitimacy requires inclusive public reason); magisterial reading claims the Gospel reveals non-negotiable truths about dignity that precede democratic deliberation. No single framework can hold both 'all dignity claims are subject to democratic contestation' and 'some dignity claims are revealed truths immune to democratic revision.'

axes.structural_delta: Irreducible disagreement over what grounds the authority to define legitimate AI governance: Gospel-grounded Social Doctrine vs. technocratic expertise vs. democratic deliberation vs. market spontaneous order
axes.primary_observable: Regulatory frameworks adopted; whose principles (Magisterial, utilitarian, democratic, libertarian) structure AI oversight institutions; which populations' interests are systematically prioritized or excluded
axes.selection_reason: Core contested kernel. All four readings are individually holdable, structurally distinct (different beneficiary/victim sets, different constraint types), and live in global AI governance debates. Kernel counts as ONE axis; all four readings proceed to generation.

axes.structural_delta: Automation and AI reshape labor markets, threatening unemployment, deskilling, and precarity. Work is not merely income but a site of human development, relational formation, and contribution to common good. Structural question: can technological transformation preserve work's dignity-conferring function?
axes.primary_observable: Employment rates in automatable sectors; wage trends for displaced vs. augmented workers; access to retraining; labor's share of income; worker participation in automation decisions
axes.selection_reason: Distinct from governance kernel (different observable: labor market structure vs. regulatory authority). High ε; directly affects families and social stability. Encyclical devotes Chapter 4 section to this. Passes independence test.

axes.human_readable: Communication Ecology and Truth as Common Good
axes.structural_delta: Digital platforms and AI-driven content curation shape collective imagination, blur truth/falsehood boundaries, enable disinformation at scale. Truth is relational (built through trust, verification, shared practices) and rational (requires evidence). Structural question: can communication infrastructure serve truth as common good or only private/factional interests?
axes.primary_observable: Prevalence of disinformation; algorithmic transparency; media concentration; public trust in institutions; access to independent journalism; educational digital literacy programs
axes.selection_reason: Distinct from work axis (different observable: information flows vs. labor markets). Encyclical treats communication as foundational to democracy and common good (Chapter 4). Moderate ε; affects political culture. Passes independence test.

axes.structural_delta: Transhumanism/posthumanism frame human limits (finitude, vulnerability, mortality) as defects to be technologically overcome. Christian humanism frames limits as sites of grace, relationship, and transcendence through communion with God. Collision: is human fulfillment found in self-enhancement or self-gift?
axes.primary_observable: Cultural narratives in tech industry; funding for enhancement research vs. care infrastructure; bioethics policy on human augmentation; public discourse on aging, disability, suffering
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: cultural/ideological rather than structural. Encyclical treats this as background worldview (Chapter 3) shaping governance debates, but it lacks independent ε—its effects are mediated through governance, work, and communication axes already selected. Rope with no direct victim set. Captured as omega.

axes.structural_delta: AI lowers threshold for lethal force (autonomous weapons, cyberattacks, predictive targeting), obscures responsibility, and normalizes conflict as inevitable. Encyclical rejects 'just war' framework as outdated; demands disarmament and diplomacy. Structural question: does AI make war more 'feasible' and thus more frequent?
axes.primary_observable: Autonomous weapons deployment; military AI R&D budgets; international arms control treaties (presence/absence); civilian casualty rates in AI-augmented conflicts; diplomatic engagement vs. military posturing
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: encyclical devotes Chapter 5 to this, but it is structurally downstream of governance kernel (how AI is governed determines whether weapons development is constrained). High ε but not independent—war axis is an application domain of the governance kernel's contested readings. Including it would over-split. Captured as high-priority omega.

axes.human_readable: Global South as Data Extraction Frontier
axes.structural_delta: Health data, genetic profiles, demographic information from structurally fragile regions become 'new rare earths'—aggregated by Northern tech firms to train models, guide investment, predict crises. Encyclical frames this as neo-colonialism. Structural question: who controls and benefits from data generated in the Global South?
axes.primary_observable: Data sovereignty laws in Global South; tech firm data collection practices; benefit-sharing agreements; access to AI-derived medical/agricultural innovations in data-source regions
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: encyclical raises this (§178) as example of new colonialism, but it is a specific instance of the universal destination of goods principle applied to data (already covered in governance kernel's magisterial reading). Not structurally independent—same observable (data control) as governance kernel, just geographically specified. Captured as omega for regional focus.

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Transhumanism vs. Christian humanism on human limits
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Cultural/ideological background. Effects mediated through governance, work, communication axes. No independent ε. Encyclical treats as worldview shaping other debates, not standalone constraint.

deferred_axes.structural_delta: AI lowers threshold for lethal force, normalizes conflict
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Application domain of governance kernel. High ε but not independent—whether AI weapons proliferate depends on which governance reading prevails. Including would over-split. Chapter 5 material captured in omega.

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Data from Global South as extractive resource for Northern tech firms
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Specific geographic instance of universal destination of goods principle (already in magisterial reading). Same observable (data control) as governance kernel. Not structurally independent. Regional focus captured in omega.

omegas.description: Does transhumanism function as a Rope (shared cultural narrative coordinating tech development) or a Piton (atrophied moral imagination unable to recognize limits as grace-sites)? Encyclical treats it as ideological substrate of technocratic paradigm, but its independent causal force vs. being epiphenomenal to economic incentives is unclear.

Is AI weaponization a distinct axis or strictly downstream of governance kernel? If magisterial reading prevails (subsidiarity + solidarity), autonomous weapons face moral prohibition. If technocratic or libertarian readings prevail, weapons development accelerates. Encyclical's Chapter 5 assumes governance determines war trajectory, but autonomous military-industrial dynamics may decouple them.

Does Global South data extraction constitute independent axis or instance of governance kernel? If data sovereignty movements succeed (democratic pluralist reading), extraction is constrained. If technocratic/market readings prevail, extraction intensifies. Encyclical flags neo-colonialism (§178) but does not develop structural independence from universal destination of goods principle.

Encyclical acknowledges Church's historical complicity in slavery (§176–177) and delayed condemnation (18 centuries). Does this pattern risk repeating with AI? If Magisterium's interpretive authority rests on continuity with Gospel, how does it guard against future apologies for present blindness to AI-enabled exploitation (e.g., invisible labor in data annotation, resource extraction for rare earths)?
omegas.source: §176–177; commitment system drift_status='functioning' assumes revision capacity, but historical lag raises vigilance question

omegas.description: Encyclical grounds solidarity in Eucharistic communion (§234–235): 'union with Christ is also union with all those to whom he gives himself.' Is this a Scaffold (builds ecclesial culture that influences broader society) or a Piton (internal ecclesial practice with no structural leverage on secular AI governance)? Mechanism linking sacramental life to political economy remains unspecified.

Subsidiarity principle (§68–72) demands decisions at lowest competent level. But AI infrastructure is inherently global (data flows, model training, platform effects). Does subsidiarity collapse at planetary scale, or does it demand new forms of nested, federated governance? Encyclical asserts principle but does not resolve scale paradox.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan applied: theological ethics (Magisterial tradition), political economy (work, inequality), communication theory (truth as common good), international relations (war, multilateralism). Dark matter probes surfaced transhumanism (Probe 1: operational medium), Global South extraction (Probe 2: absence), and Eucharistic solidarity mechanism (Probe 3: beneficiary of framing). Kernel/reading decomposition applied per §1.3-K: AI governance is genuinely contested (four individually-holdable readings with distinct beneficiary/victim structures and axiom contradictions). Readings drawn from multiple traditions (Catholic, utilitarian, liberal democratic, libertarian) per lens diversity requirement. All selected axes pass §3 pairwise independence test.
